rule.what_the_ceiling_is: The most anchor events the peer side could reach if every unresolved question resolved favourably. A sample-size feasibility count, the same category as the 342 anchor events.
rule.what_the_ceiling_is_not: Eligibility. No pair here has passed pair_eligibility, the ceiling run supplies peer price availability as a stated hypothetical rather than a measurement, and CeilingReport has no eligible field.
rule.measured_vs_ceiling: Both are published. The measured join is the honest state and returns zero, all denied on P5. The ceiling exists because P5 denying everything hides whether P1 and P3 would have denied it too.
rule.worklist_counts_are_anchor_side_only: A candidate's count is this anchor's shock-carrying events after the earliest filing that disclosed the counterparty. No peer ticker or price is involved, which is why it is derivable now.
rule.name_resolution_refuses: Fuzzy matching and scored matching. A wrong ticker is fabricated linkage wearing a number and it fails silently. Ambiguous names, self-links and near-misses are left UNRESOLVED for the curator.
rule.every_resolution_needs_lineage_review: SEC's ticker map describes companies as they are today; the names come from filings made years earlier. Caremark RX and OfficeMax were both rejected on exactly this ground -- a merger is not a rename -- so no row is promoted automatically.
rule.not_a_curated_map: The worklist's columns are provably disjoint from curated_linkage.REQUIRED_FIELDS, so load_curated_linkage refuses it on the header. refuse_if_curated_schema enforces the same thing at build time.
rule.resolution_is_survivorship_biased_by_con: Names are resolved against SEC's list of CURRENT filers, so a delisted, merged-away, taken-private or never-US-listed counterparty cannot resolve at all. See `resolution_survivorship`.
rule.opens_no_gate: The display gate is CLOSED, C4 MET, four denials. C2 counts eligible anchor events and this supplies none; C2 and C3 move together or not at all.

what_this_is: How far the peer side can reach with the linkage that exists today, and which unreviewed candidates would extend it. A feasibility measurement of the SAMPLE, not of the hypothesis.
what_this_is_not: Evidence about supply-chain transmission. No peer return has been measured, no pair is eligible, and the display gate is CLOSED with the eligible-event count at zero.

resolution_survivorship.why_this_is_structural: company_tickers.json lists companies that file and trade today. A counterparty that was delisted, merged away, taken private or never a US filer cannot resolve against it at all -- by construction, not by imperfect matching. Widening the matcher cannot fix this; only a source that includes former registrants can.
resolution_survivorship.why_it_biases_toward_the_hypothesis: peer_price_data_policy's own reasoning applies one level earlier. The peers most likely to have disappeared are those acquired or taken private, and acquisition is frequently CAUSED by the commercial relationship under study, so the unreachable counterparties are not missing at random.
resolution_survivorship.what_it_does_not_claim: That every unresolved name is a delisted company. Some are ambiguous, some foreign-listed, some brands or subsidiaries that were never registrants. The method cannot tell those apart from survivors, which is why the whole set is the exposure.
resolution_survivorship.not_a_property_of_the_rule: This measures the RESOLUTION METHOD, not the anchor universe and not the peer-eligibility rule. It is a fact about how the worklist was built on this date.

the_binding_constraint: Prices, not curation -- REVERSED from every prior version of this artifact. The curated map now reaches 215 anchor events against a floor of 193, so curation no longer caps the sample below the floor. That ceiling ASSUMES peer prices exist. None do: the measured join yields 0 eligible pairs and 0 anchor events with a peer. A peer price source is now the binding constraint, and no such source is registered.

worklist.why_incremental_matters: A candidate duplicating an existing edge at a LATER as_of date has a large gross count and buys nothing. Two resolved rows are exactly that, both MCK -> CVS behind the curated 2013-05-07 edge, and they are flagged dominated_by_curated_map.
worklist.union_is_not_a_sum: Candidates on one anchor cover overlapping stretches of the same event list, so summing max_anchor_events would double-count heavily. The union is the only honest total.
worklist.what_the_union_means: The queue CONTAINS enough material to reach the floor. It does not make any of it eligible: no candidate is curated, no as_of is ratified, every resolution needs lineage review, and no peer price source exists.

what_changed_from_2026_09_02_v2: PROVENANCE ONLY. Every number in this artifact is identical to _v2: ceiling 215, measured 0 eligible pairs, the same by_anchor split, the same worklist rows. Nothing was remeasured.

The map in force moved from HYP04_Linkage_Map_v1.1.csv to v1.2, which raises date_confidence on NVDA->MSFT (low -> high) and JBL->CSCO (medium -> high). Those grades ask whether the as_of is really the floor; the 2026-09-02 walk read the previously invisible 10-K405s sitting before both dates and neither names its counterparty, so both are now floors across a COMPLETE annual-report series. The grades recorded an open question that has since been measured.

date_confidence has no consumer wired (recorded inert by the 2026-08-18 linkage-source decision), which is exactly why the ceiling is unchanged and why this revision exists only so a dated artifact does not cite a map that is no longer in force.
what_changed_from_2026_09_02: The review queue is rebuilt from a corrected EDGAR walk. Both walk entry points filtered on form == '10-K' exactly, which excluded 10-K405 (a valid annual report 1996-2003) and 10-KT entirely: 56 annual reports across 25 tickers had never been examined. They have been, and the walk now reads 1306 filings instead of 1250, with zero retrieval failures.

The correction moved NO curated as_of_date. NVDA's three newly-visible 10-K405s (1999-04-29, 2000, 2001-04-27) do not name Microsoft, so NVDA->MSFT's as_of of 2004-03-29 is now a PROVEN floor across a complete annual-report series rather than the earliest of an incomplete one. The same holds for JBL->CSCO at 2002-11-25 after JBL's 1999 10-K405 was read.
One counterparty name is newly visible across the whole expansion: NVDA / Celestica, earliest 2001-04-27, from a 10-K405 the old filter could not see.

XOM now carries a stated refusal instead of a zero. It resolves through company_tickers.json to CIK 2115436 'ExxonMobil Holdings Corp', a post-reorganisation registrant with no filing history, and the previous walk recorded that as filings_on_record 0 with no error -- indistinguishable from a filer that disclosed nothing. It is excluded from counts rather than counted as zero.
The ceiling itself is UNCHANGED at 215. It is a function of the curated map, the calendar and the shocks, none of which moved; the walk feeds the candidate worklist, not the curated reach.
what_changed_from_2026_08_31_v3: The curated map moved from HYP04_Linkage_Map_v1.0.csv (2 edges) to v1.1 (7 edges). The owner curated the five machine-prepared draft rows -- JBL->CSCO, JBL->AAPL, JBL->BB, NVDA->MSFT, INTC->HPQ -- supplying the five fields no derivation can supply. v1.1 is the UNION: v1.0's two rows are carried through unchanged, because this artifact's reader takes the newest map and a v1.1 holding only the new rows would have dropped them.
The method is unchanged. Same calendar, same shocks, same review queue, same rule. Every difference below follows from the map.

the_binding_constraint is now DERIVED from whether the ceiling reaches the floor, instead of being a hardcoded string. It has reversed: through v3 curation bound at a ceiling of 54; it now reads 215 against a floor of 193, and prices bind.
A ceiling above the floor is still not an eligible event. The measured join yields zero eligible pairs, the display gate is CLOSED with four denials, and C2 counts eligible events only.
what_changed_from_v2: Adds resolution_survivorship. Names are resolved against SEC's company_tickers.json, which lists companies that file and trade TODAY, so a delisted, merged-away, taken-private or never-US-listed counterparty cannot resolve BY CONSTRUCTION. The resolved set is therefore a survivorship-biased sample of the queue. Measured, because peer_price_data_policy permits a survivors-only restriction only if its bias is stated, and a statement of bias needs a number.
what_changed_from_v1: The name normaliser no longer strips HOLDING/HOLDINGS/GROUP. They are not legal forms: they separate a holding company from its operating company and a successor vehicle from its predecessor. v1 resolved ADBE's 2006 disclosure of 'Ingram Micro' onto INGM (Ingram Micro Holding Corp, CIK 1897762), the 2024 re-IPO vehicle. That row is now UNRESOLVED, which is correct, and the resolved count falls by one.

Candidate counts are now reported INCREMENTAL to the curated map as well as gross, and rows the map already covers are flagged dominated_by_curated_map. v1's headline union of 231 counted events the curated edge already reaches.
Rows are ranked by incremental opportunity rather than gross.
opens_no_gate: The display gate is CLOSED, C4 MET, four denials. C2 counts ELIGIBLE anchor events; this artifact supplies none, and C2 and C3 move together or not at all.
